Top Japanese title: 「文を結ぶ2つのリズム」

Teach coordination versus subordination. Equal partners linked by and/but/or/so share the same grammatical level; a subordinate clause adds time, reason, condition, concession, etc. to a main clause. Show that a fronted subordinate clause is normally followed by a comma.

Original examples:
• Leo cooked, and Mia set the table. 「同じ強さの2文」
• The path was steep, but we kept climbing. 「逆方向の等位接続」
• When the bell rang, everyone stood up. 「時の背景→主節」
• We stayed inside because the wind was fierce. 「主節に理由を追加」

Central diagram: equal two-car train vs main locomotive + subordinate context carriage; show clause can move: “When..., main.” / “Main when....”

Mini practice: punctuate “If the gate is open we can enter.” Answer: “If the gate is open, we can enter.” Reason: 「前置き従属節と主節の境目」.

Takeaway: 「並べる接続と、主節に背景を添える接続を見分ける」.
